reference_sql:
SELECT date_trunc('quarter', order_date) AS order_quarter,
       SUM(net_revenue_eur) AS net_revenue_eur
FROM sales
GROUP BY 1
alternatives: SELECT CAST(date_trunc('quarter', order_date) AS DATE) AS order_quarter, SUM(net_revenue_eur) AS net_revenue_eur FROM sales GROUP BY date_trunc('quarter', order_date)
SELECT make_date(year(order_date), 3 * quarter(order_date) - 2, 1) AS order_quarter, SUM(net_revenue_eur) AS net_revenue_eur FROM sales GROUP BY year(order_date), quarter(order_date)

other_way.sql: SELECT make_date(year(order_date), 3 * quarter(order_date) - 2, 1) AS order_quarter, SUM(net_revenue_eur) AS net_revenue_eur FROM sales GROUP BY year(order_date), quarter(order_date)
other_way.tradeoff: Building the date from the year and the quarter works, but date_trunc names the period in one call and cannot get the month wrong.
